newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Zagrebacka hits record high. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Croatian Zagrebacka hits record high. [CORRECTED 17:25 GMT]

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed to lower in moderate business on Tuesday, with fully-listed Zagrebacka Banka stealing the spotlight by hitting its all-time high at 2,180 kuna.
Traders forecast a more favourable general trend for the week ahead, with buoyant activity and higher prices for most stocks as the market was seen to be in a phase of growth.
"Zagrebacka's rise was expected. Demand for its shares is huge, and offer is getting smaller and smaller," said Marijan Palic of Auctor brokerage.
Zagrebacka led gainers on Tuesday, climbing 120 kuna to 2,180. Its GDRs, issued ten for each share, fetched $36.375 on London's Seaq International, up from $35.3125 where it closed on Monday.
"Zagrebacka's price (in London on Tuesday) is fantastic. It could rise to 2,300 kuna in Zagreb," said Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage.

The bank offered a good long-term prospect, as its favourable credit rating will enable it to get access to the cheaper capital abroad to finance potentially profitable tourist firms in its portfolio, including Istraturist and Jadranturist, Zelimorski said.

"Istraturist saw intense trading today. But its price is too low, given that Zagrebacka partly owns it," Zelimorski said. The stock inched down three kuna to 200, selling 1,242 units. Jadranturist also lost two kuna to 303.
Nine of 19 active issues fell, five rose and five were flat. Volume fell to 12,074 shares from 17,259. Turnover was almost three times lower at 6.8 million kuna.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva fell 25 kuna to 460 on volume of 1,337 units. Its 5/1 GDRs traded lower in London at $15.385 in mid-afternoon.
"Pliva's fall is surprising both in London and Zagreb, since its business results for 1996 were far better than the previous year," Palic said.
But he saw it as a short-term decline, most probably caused by some investors who decided to sell its shares after it traded on high volume in London.
Varazdinska Banka second issue, recently listed in the top bracket of the Zagreb bourse, alongside Pliva and Zagrebacka, lost 30 kuna to 1,330, with 22 units traded.

Most active issue was food processor Podravka, inching down 0.50 kuna to 305 (corrects from 205), with 3,986 shares changing hands. Traders said the stock should remain stable and saw it as unlikely to fall under 300 kuna.
Top decliner was shipper Atlantska Plovidba, edging down 10 kuna to 110 and selling 50 shares.
Chocolate maker Kras and hotelier Riviera were also on the losing side, both falling 10 kuna to 450 and 1,480 kuna, respectively.
